A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniCalli work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and recognition experiments, component ablations, a 20-participant user study, and evaluations on oracle bone script and Egyptian hieroglyphs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CalliBench recognition results, a CalliReader comparison and practical generation examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the backbone, asymmetric noising, losses, box-map modeling, Duplicate RoPE, conditional dropout and joint training. Appendix E supplies previously missing recognition-readout and embedding implementation details, without establishing that the underlying procedures changed.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds evaluation on CalliBench's Easy subset, extending recognition coverage to the modern artistic fonts and contemporary calligraphy described there. The original Chinese calligraphy, oracle bone and Egyptian datasets remain. The application gallery supplies further examples of the retained generation task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds CalliReader to the existing held-out recognition comparison. The new CalliBench comparison uses the six recognition comparators already evaluated in v1; generation and oracle bone comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The added CalliBench experiment uses the Easy subset and reports precision, recall, F1 and NED in a described zero-shot transfer setting. Existing training budgets, recognition splits and user-study procedures remain unchanged. The expanded ablation-baseline description discloses settings rather than demonstrating a revised experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a distribution-shift evaluation from historical training styles to modern calligraphy. Appendix J adds practical case studies involving poetry scrolls, blessings and marriage certificates. The component and dropout ablations are retained unchanged; relocating the oracle bone illustration adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same user-rating means and standard deviations. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests; its new benchmark results use point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds CalliReader results, including 0.533 overall accuracy and 0.658 on Running/Xing. New Table 6 reports CalliBench F1 scores of 0.498 for UniCalli, 0.593 for GOT-OCR2.0 and 0.534 for Qwen-2.5-VL-7B. Appendix J adds generated examples. Existing numerical results remain unchanged; the new benchmark does not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds formal definitions of the character-reference library and cosine-nearest-neighbor recognition rule in Equations 4–5, plus the feature-level modality offset in Equation 6. Section 3's existing mathematics remains unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow several page-level composition and unification claims to column-level claims. The dataset, unified learning, generative performance and ancient-script transfer contributions remain. The conclusion still retains its broader page-level wording.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes white-patch artifacts to damaged historical rubbings and binarization, interprets CalliBench results through a modern-versus-ancient domain gap, and presents practical applications as evidence of production readiness. Table 4's caption also newly interprets perceptual-metric improvements as avoiding pixel-averaging mode collapse. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E fills substantial implementation gaps concerning character retrieval, reference-library construction and zero-initialized modality embeddings before attention projections. Section 4.2 specifies the generation-only FLUX baseline, and Appendix J discloses layout, color and compositing post-processing. Conversely, v2 removes the abstract's direct code/data link; this does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MCCD citation, Zhao et al. (2025), and positions CalliBench as an available public alternative with a different data distribution. The main related-work discussion and its relationships to earlier generation and recognition approaches are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order remain intact. Changes include localized rewriting in Sections 3.3 and 4.2, column-level terminology, the publication-status header, and appendix organization accommodating the new material. Existing appendix content is retained under updated labels.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document into a narrower conference layout, resizing and repositioning figures and tables. It adds a CalliReader column, the CalliBench table and the application gallery in Figures 19–27. The former main-text oracle bone Figure 6 is relocated as appendix Figure 10, rather than removed.

improvement.justification: The added specialist comparator and external CalliBench evaluation strengthen recognition evidence beyond the original internal test set, while Appendix E makes important implementation steps substantially clearer. These are useful, bounded gains with the core results unchanged. Removing the direct code/data link weakens access information, and the application demonstrations provide limited support for the new production-readiness interpretation.
